stem: Five friends P, Q, R, S, T are seated in a straight row, all facing North. The following are known: R is at the leftmost seat. Q is seated immediately to the right of P. S is seated immediately to the right of Q. T is at the rightmost seat. Who occupies the middle seat?

per_option_rationale.rationale: R is at position 1 (leftmost). T is at position 5 (rightmost). P, Q, S fill positions 2, 3, 4 in that order because Q is right of P and S is right of Q. So the row is R, P, Q, S, T and the middle seat (position 3) is Q.
Placing P in the middle (position 3) ignores that S must be immediately right of Q, pushing Q and S to positions 4 and 5, which contradicts T being at the rightmost seat.
Reversing the chain so that P is right of Q and Q is right of S gives the order R, S, Q, P, T, placing S in the middle, but this reverses the stated direction of adjacency.
Reading R as the middle person ignores the explicit clue that R is at the leftmost (not middle) seat.

explanation: R fixes position 1 (leftmost) and T fixes position 5 (rightmost). The chain P-Q-S (each immediately right of the previous) occupies positions 2, 3, 4. Middle seat = position 3 = Q.

explanation_sections.punchline: Fix the two end anchors first, then slot in the chain to find the middle.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply clues most-certain-first: R at leftmost (pos 1), T at rightmost (pos 5). Remaining positions 2-4 must hold P, Q, S with Q right of P and S right of Q: P(2), Q(3), S(4). Middle = pos 3 = Q.
explanation_sections.lesson: Anchor the ends first, then build the interior chain from adjacency clues.
explanation_sections.timing: Under 45 seconds. The trap is reversing the adjacency chain, placing S in the middle.
